overall_reason: The textbook generated SaaS page: placeholder brand 'SaaSify', 'Streamline Your Workflow Like Never Before', a four-figure stat band, a borrowed logo wall (Stripe, Notion, Linear, Vercel, Figma), three icon feature cards, three five-star testimonials from stock names, three pricing tiers, a 'Ready to Transform' CTA band and a link-farm footer; nine stock sections in stock order and no product shown.

findings.where: whole page, tiles 1440-00 to 03 and dom-1440.json text
findings.evidence: Failed T-STOCK-ORDER (9 stock sections): centred hero > stat band (10K+, 99.9%, 50M+, 4.9) > 'TRUSTED BY INDUSTRY LEADERS' logo strip > 'Everything You Need to Scale' three equal icon cards > 'Loved by Teams Worldwide' three testimonial cards > 'Simple, Transparent Pricing' three tiers with 'Most Popular' > 'Ready to Transform Your Workflow?' CTA band > four-column link-farm footer. Failed T-DEFAULT-AGENT: 'landing page for a workflow automation SaaS' produces this verbatim.
findings.before: Stock SaaS sequence with no product visible
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: what the product automates, for whom, and a real screenshot]; build the first screen around one workflow shown end to end.
findings.why: Seven or more stock sections reads as generated.

findings.evidence: Failed T-FIVE-SECOND: the hero says 'automate tasks, boost productivity, and scale their operations' but never which tasks or for which team; there is no product image anywhere on the page. A visitor cannot tell what SaaSify does.
findings.before: Streamline Your Workflow Like Never Before
findings.after: A head naming the job, e.g. '[Product] turns [specific trigger] into [specific outcome] for [team]'. [DATA NEEDED: the actual job]
findings.why: What it is and who it is for are unanswered on the first screen.

findings.evidence: 'TRUSTED BY INDUSTRY LEADERS' over Stripe, Notion, Linear, Vercel and Figma wordmarks. These are real companies placed as customers of a placeholder product with no source; the sweep caught '10,000+ teams' but not the logo wall.
findings.before: Trusted by: Stripe, Notion, Linear, Vercel, Figma
findings.after: Remove the strip until there are customers who have agreed to be named. [DATA NEEDED: permitted customer logos]
findings.why: Invented logo walls using real brands are an integrity and impersonation failure (INT-103).

findings.evidence: Three five-star cards from 'Sarah Mitchell, VP Operations, TechCorp', 'James Chen, CTO, ScaleUp Inc', 'Amanda Rodriguez, Founder, GrowthLab': stock names, placeholder companies, initials avatars, and quotes built to formula ('reduced our manual work by 80%', 'ROI was visible within the first month', 'Best investment we've made').
findings.before: "SaaSify reduced our manual work by 80%." — Sarah Mitchell, TechCorp
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: real, attributable quotes], or remove the section.
findings.why: Fake people and invented outcome numbers (INT-102, INT-104).

findings.evidence: Failed T-RIVAL-NAME on every heading: 'Everything You Need to Scale', 'Loved by Teams Worldwide', 'Simple, Transparent Pricing', 'Ready to Transform Your Workflow?' and the sub-line 'work smarter, not harder' stay true for Zapier, Make or n8n. All headings are in Title Case, a second default.
findings.after: Heads that state a checkable fact about this product. [DATA NEEDED: differentiators]
findings.why: Concept capped at 5: no line belongs to this business.

findings.evidence: Failed T-DELETION: lightning bolt, bar chart and padlock icons in tiles above 'Instant Automation', 'Real-time Analytics', 'Enterprise Security'. Each icon is the literal stock glyph for its heading and adds nothing; 'Bank-level encryption, SOC 2 compliance' is an unbacked claim.
findings.before: ⚡ Instant Automation / 📊 Real-time Analytics / 🔒 Enterprise Security
findings.after: Drop the icon tiles; replace the three cards with one real workflow screenshot and a short list; state SOC 2 only with a report link. [DATA NEEDED: SOC 2 status]
findings.why: Icon tile above every card heading on equal cards (SLP-003, SLP-005).

strengths: Pricing tiers state concrete limits (5 users / 100 automations, 25 users / unlimited) that a buyer can compare; nothing else on the page is specific.
not_investigated: Render fidelity: Tailwind v3 config was ignored by the v4 shim, so the Pro tier, CTA band, primary buttons and footer render white on white; colours, fonts (Poppins/Open Sans intended) and the CTA band layout were judged from dom-1440.json text, not the screenshots
slop words, '10,000+ teams', '99.9% Uptime' and the stat band: reported by the sweep, not repeated
